questions.question: What must you NOT do to a moving vehicle ahead of you inside crossing zig-zags?
options: Leave a two-second gap behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans overtaking any leading moving or stopped vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

questions.question: When passing a cyclist riding past parked cars, why leave extra room?
options: A parked car door could suddenly open into the cyclist's path
The cyclist must ride on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 notes cyclists ride away from parked cars to avoid opening doors.

questions.question: What is the main danger of driving too close to the car in front?
options: You may not have time to stop if they brake suddenly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 warns that tailgating leaves no room to stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do before signalling to pull over and stop?
options: Check your mirrors to see who is behind you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 works with mirror checks so others understand your signal.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a dual carriageway with a central barrier?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 70 mph for cars on dual carriageways unless signed lower.

questions.question: What shape is a red-and-white Give Way sign?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 uses the inverted red-and-white triangle for Give Way.

questions.question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when taking an exit to the right?
options: No signal until after you leave
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to signal right on approach for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: What signal must you give just before leaving any roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal as you prepare to leave a roundabout.

questions.question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

questions.question: On a two-lane roundabout, where should you position your car?
options: Centred cleanly inside your marked lane
Hugging the grass island on every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to keep cleanly within their lane markings.

questions.question: When taking the first exit on the left at a roundabout, which lane do you choose?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to approach in the left-hand lane for the first exit.

questions.question: When turning right out of a side road onto a main road, who must you give way to?
options: Traffic coming from both right and left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 requires checking and giving way to both directions when turning right.

questions.question: Before moving back to the left lane after overtaking, what must you be sure of?
options: There is plenty of room ahead of the passed vehicle
The car behind flashes its lights
You are going at least 70 mph
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns not to cut in front of the vehicle you overtook.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, which side should you look to first for circulating traffic?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 tells you to give way to traffic coming from your right.

questions.question: How do you signal on approach when taking the first exit to the left?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal on approach for the first exit.

questions.question: If you are taking the third exit, when do you switch to a left exit signal?
options: Just after passing the second exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 times the left signal right after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: Where should the central island of a UK roundabout always stay?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 keeps the central island on your right as you travel clockwise.

questions.question: Does the zig-zag no-overtaking rule apply at signal-controlled crossings like pelican crossings too?
options: Yes, it applies at all pedestrian crossings with zig-zags
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies to zebra, pelican, puffin, and toucan crossings with zig-zags.

questions.question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction and leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 requires waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

questions.question: In wet or windy weather, how should you adjust your overtaking gap past a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than usual
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises extra clearance in poor weather or strong side winds.

questions.question: What happens to your view ahead when you leave a proper two-second gap?
options: You can see past the vehicle ahead and spot hazards earlier
You see less of the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 notes a wider gap improves your view of road hazards.

questions.question: If you signal early, does that give you the right to pull out?
options: Yes, other drivers must stop for you
No, you must still wait until it is safe
Yes, if you signal for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds drivers that signals show intent and never give priority.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a single-lane-each-way rural road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 60 mph for cars on single rural roads without lower signs.

questions.question: If you approach a roundabout in the wrong lane and traffic is beside you, what is safest?
options: Follow your lane safely and turn around later
Cut across the car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids sudden lane changes across circulating traffic.

questions.question: What if a bus stops just before a zebra crossing to let someone cross? May you pass the bus?
options: No, you must wait behind the bus
Yes, pass slowly on the right
Yes, if you sound your horn
Only if no stripes are visible
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans passing the lead vehicle because it can hide pedestrians.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction. Your exit road is clear, but oncoming cars block your turn. May you wait in the box?
options: Yes, you may wait in the box to turn right
Only if you turn on hazard lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 makes a specific exception when turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a large lorry is in front of you, why should you stay well back?
options: So you can see past it and its driver can see you in their mirrors
To stay in its blind spot
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 helps you stay visible and see further ahead.

questions.question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

questions.question: Can you drive above the speed limit briefly while overtaking?
options: Yes, for up to five seconds
No, you must never exceed the speed limit
Yes, if no cameras are nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 makes clear that speed limits are the legal maximum at all times.

questions.question: Before turning left soon after passing a cyclist, what must you check?
options: Do not overtake and immediately cut across the cyclist's path
Always turn sharply in front of them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 182 warn against 'left hooks' across cyclists.

questions.question: When can the right-hand approach lane also be used for going straight ahead?
options: When road signs or lane arrows direct straight-ahead traffic into that lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 notes that signs and markings can override the default left lane.

questions.question: When turning left from a side road onto a main road, which direction is the main danger first?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 checks right first for nearside flow, and left for overtaking traffic.

questions.question: When two lanes merge into one, how should you treat a driver alongside you?
options: Leave space and merge in turn safely
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and merging advice promote safe, courteous lane changes.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, does the same give-way-to-the-right rule apply?
options: Yes, give way to traffic from your right just like a full roundabout
Traffic from the left goes first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and 188 apply the same give-way-to-the-right rule at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: When turning right at a small mini-roundabout, what mistake do learners sometimes make?
options: Cutting the corner on the wrong side of the white circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 warn drivers not to cut across the wrong side of the central marking.

questions.question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car, when do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns that early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

questions.question: What does a round white sign with a black diagonal stripe mean?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 links the national speed limit sign to 60 or 70 mph limits.

questions.question: On a spiral roundabout, how do the lane markings guide you?
options: They gradually lead you outward toward your exit
They mean you must stop on the island
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises following lane markings that guide you cleanly out to your exit.

questions.question: What should you do if a lorry beside you needs extra width to turn on a roundabout?
options: Hold back and give the lorry plenty of room instead of sitting alongside it
Pull right beside its rear wheels
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 221 warn that long vehicles swing wide across lanes on roundabouts.

questions.question: At a tiny mini-roundabout with little space, should you still signal your turn?
options: Yes, signal clearly in good time before entering
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 188 still require clear approach signals at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, why can it be hard to give a separate left exit signal?
options: The junction is very small, so keep your focus on steering safely if tight
Left signals are banned at mini-roundabouts
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 188 note there is less time to signal exit at very small mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: When two exit lanes merge after a roundabout, how should you leave?
options: Stay in your exit lane cleanly, then merge smoothly when safe
Squeeze both cars side by side into one lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps exits orderly until lanes merge safely downstream.

questions.question: Why is a right signal on approach helpful to drivers waiting at the left-hand entrance?
options: It warns them you are staying on the roundabout past their exit
It tells them to pull out in front of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 helps waiting drivers judge whether you will cross their path.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to exit. What must you check before signalling left and moving out?
options: Your left mirror and blind spot for vehicles on your left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires checking left before moving across to exit.

questions.question: Why are zig-zag lines painted on BOTH the approach and exit sides of a crossing?
options: To keep views clear in both directions and stop overtaking or parking near the stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 keeps both sides of the crossing clear for pedestrians and drivers.

questions.question: Are half-box junctions sometimes painted on only one side of a T-junction?
options: Yes, to keep that side clear for turning traffic
No, they are always full squares
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 covers full and half-box yellow markings at busy junctions.

questions.question: On a 50 mph rural road, why is 1.5 metres often not enough when passing a cyclist?
options: High speed creates strong air turbulence, so give even more room
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 explicitly requires even more space at speeds over 30 mph.
